headline: Steady demand lifts results but EPS guidance is trimmed
summary_short: Revenue rose 1.0% y/y to $555.1M and diluted EPS grew 13.0% to $1.04, helped by a ~$35M gain on the disposition of a Raleigh community; MAA lowered full-year EPS guidance to $3.96-$4.20 (from $4.18-$4.50) while holding Core FFO guidance at an $8.53 midpoint.
summary_long: Revenue grew 1.0% y/y to $555.1M despite Same Store revenue slipping 0.3%, as lease-up and development communities (MAA Cathedral Arts, MAA Plaza Midwood) added Non-Same-Store revenue. Net income rose 12.6% to $121.8M and diluted EPS grew 13.0% to $1.04, driven by a ~$35.3M gain on the Raleigh, NC community disposition, partly offset by higher interest expense ($53.1M vs $45.1M). Same Store blended lease rate growth accelerated to 0.7%. MAA repurchased $50M of stock. Full-year EPS guidance was cut to $3.96-$4.20 (mid $4.08, from mid $4.34), while Core FFO and Core AFFO guidance were held at $8.53 and $7.50 midpoints; Same Store revenue-growth guidance was lowered to a 0.10% midpoint (from 0.55%).

drivers.explanation: Total revenue grew despite Same Store revenue falling 0.3% y/y, as newly delivered and lease-up communities such as MAA Cathedral Arts and MAA Plaza Midwood added incremental Non-Same-Store revenue.
Not disclosed as a discrete line; per the release's Same Store operating table, Same Store expenses rose 0.8% y/y while Same Store revenue fell 0.3%, squeezing property-level margin.
Not explained by the company as such; per the income statement, depreciation and amortization rose to $162.5M from $153.5M y/y, outpacing the modest revenue gain and pulling operating income down.
The release's own EBITDA reconciliation shows net income rising to $124.8M from $110.9M plus higher depreciation and amortization ($162.5M vs $153.5M), lifting EBITDA to $341.0M from $310.1M.

CEO cited steady demand and disciplined expense management; the release also shows a $35.3M gain on the Raleigh community disposition versus a $0.1M loss a year ago, partly offset by higher interest expense.
Tracks the 12.6% net income gain; diluted weighted-average shares also fell slightly to 116.1M from 117.2M, reflecting this quarter's $50M of share repurchases.

CEO: results 'exceeded our expectations due to steady demand and continued disciplined expense management,' with accelerating new-lease pricing trends. Full-year EPS and Same Store revenue-growth guidance were nonetheless lowered.
